Let me look at how `xmlIsPubidChar_tab` is used in the parser and how the input buffer relates to it. The key insight from the README is that the OOB read happens "before the global table xmlIsPubidChar_tab". This means the hash function reads a byte at an address that is one byte before the start of `xmlIsPubidChar_tab`.

Let me look at the `xmlParseNCNameComplex` function more carefully. The issue is likely that when the name is at the very end of the input buffer, `xmlDictHashName` reads past the end of the buffer. But how does that relate to `xmlIsPubidChar_tab`?

Actually, let me reconsider. The `xmlDictHashName` function reads `data[i]` in a loop. If the string data is not null-terminated and the buffer ends, it reads into adjacent memory. The README says the OOB read is "before the global table" - this could mean the string data is stored in a buffer that is located right after `xmlIsPubidChar_tab` in memory, and reading past the end of the string goes into the table.

Wait, actually re-reading: "reads one byte out-of-bounds before the global table xmlIsPubidChar_tab". This means the read address is one byte *before* the start of the table. So the string data pointer points to `xmlIsPubidChar_tab - 1` or the string ends right at `xmlIsPubidChar_tab - 1`.

Hmm, let me think about this differently. Let me look at how the parser input buffer is allocated. In libxml2, the input buffer is typically allocated with extra space for a null terminator. Let me check:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<｜｜DSML｜｜=command>cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul && grep -n "xmlBufCreate\|xmlBufAdd\|xmlBufGrow" buf.c | head -20 && echo "===" && grep -n "xmlParserInputBufferCreate\|xmlBufCreate" parser.c | head -20</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
